feedback: Before this robot races, the baseline (iteration 0) gives the only evidence. The oval finished in all 20 trials, but the s-bend and slalom both ended off track at progress 0.17 and 0.12, with max_error about 0.061 m, right at the 0.06 m limit. This points to the array not holding the line on sharp bends, not to a general speed problem. For the controller, I kept the weights in sensor order because the array is symmetric, and I raised kp and kd because a narrower track gives more turn per PWM and the wider array gives larger offsets to steer against. What the next race shows decides the next change. If the s-bend or slalom still lose the line with max_error near 0.06 m, the limit is likely turn rate or sensor coverage, so try sensor_size 0.016 to close the 4 mm gaps left by 16 mm pitch. If the robot completes but steering_oscillation rises well above the baseline 0.14, the 0.10 m track is probably overshooting, so widen it back toward 0.11 m. If the oval is no longer finished or completion_time exceeds 3 s, the 0.5 kg mass or 0.033 m radius is not the limit, so keep the wider array and revisit base_speed instead.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events stay at 1 on the s-bend or slalom with max_error near 0.06 m, change sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 so the 16 mm pitch leaves no gaps across the 25 mm tape. The baseline's outer pair at +/-0.024 m showed max_error 0.061 m, so this checks whether the array is still losing coverage.

If steering_oscillation rises well above the baseline 0.14 on a completed run, move wheel_track from 0.10 back toward 0.11 m. The narrower track raised turn gain, and that may now overshoot, as the controller was raised to kp 2.8.

If the oval fails to finish or completion_time exceeds 3 s, keep the wider array and the 0.5 kg mass, and test wheel_radius 0.035 m. This recovers top speed without changing the sensor layout that addresses the s-bend and slalom failures.
